text:
emma ng: Heads-up — I sketched a small proposal to simplify the runtime auth path between customer API keys and internal service actors. TL;DR: a compact authn bridge that normalizes inbound keys to a stable runtime claim set so routing + RBAC can consume one shape.

raj patel: curious — can you paste the minimal shape?

emma ng: sure. idea is <service_claim> + optional delegations. example header:```
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
X-Redwood-Actor: svc:ingest/ingest-worker:instance-42
X-Redwood-Delegation: svc:proxy/ingest-proxy->svc:ingest/ingest-worker
```

miguel ramos: that X-Redwood-Delegation looks like it could explode. how do we prevent combinatorial growth in graph checks? :thinking:

emma ng: agree, we limit to 1 delegation hop for runtime routing. longer chains are resolved at issuance time and turned into a single concise claim.

linda choi: operational question: how does this interact with current API keys vs project-scoped keys? we still need org/project boundaries enforced.

emma ng: plan: issuer (api key service) emits the compact claim with fields: issuer_id, audience, scope_set (projects/org ids), actor_type, expiry. RBAC will check scope_set + role mapping. keys that are project-scoped get a single project id in scope_set.

kevin taylor: sounds fine but migration pain — existing services parse raw API keys and do custom logic. can we offer a compatibility shim?

emma ng: yes — runtime will expose a small shim that accepts old header shapes and maps them to the compact claim at the edge (authn layer). shim lives in auth-proxy and is feature-flagged per service.

raj patel: what about caching/verifying claims? we shouldn't call token-introspect on every request.

miguel ramos: we plan short-lived signed JWTs from issuer for compact claims. runtime verifies signature + caches per-jti for TTL. fallback to introspect only on miss.

linda choi: JWTs are great but key rotation and KMS integration are required. ops-bot, can you confirm current rotation cadence?

ops-bot: Current issuer key rotation window: 24h active key, 7d retired keys kept for validation. Rotation is automated via KMS.

kevin taylor: ok. enforcement: RBAC will use roles + explicit project allow list. Do we keep global roles that ignore project scope?

emma ng: yes — two axes: role grants + scope_set. Role ‘org-admin’ short-circuits project checks only if scope_set includes the org id. No wildcard global bypass.

miguel ramos: edge case — async background jobs that run across projects. They get a service principal with multi-project scope_set. We need tooling to limit cardinality.

linda choi: operationally we should cap scope_set size (e.g., <=10 projects) and require review for larger.

emma ng: agreed. I'll add that to the proposal.

raj patel: last Q — rollout plan?

emma ng: rollout sketch: 1) issuer emits signed compact JWT opt-in for a subset of keys, 2) deploy auth-proxy shim to accept/translate old shapes, feature-flag per service, 3) enable RBAC checks against claims, 4) retire old ad-hoc parsers. Canary with low-traffic services first.

kevin taylor: please add migration checklist items: SDK updates, auth-proxy helm changes, canary services list.

emma ng: will do. thanks all — filing a short RFC follow-up with the details and a migration checklist. :thumbsup:
